correctness_confidence.basis: All mathematical identities and worked values visible in the PDF verify independently: Theorem 5's integer expansion, Theorem 6's c^2=-p collapse, Eq. (1) and H(x) evaluations for p=13, 17, 19, 29 (C01, C02, C09, C10), h_{-23}=3 and det(M)^2=-23^5 (C06), norm-1 unit power \varepsilon_{229}^3 = 1710+113\sqrt{229} (C12), and Fig. 2-3 logarithmic bars. Only the PDF summary is inspected; external Lean/Python sources are unexamined.

novelty.basis: The manuscript explicitly claims no primary mathematical discoveries, attributing all theorems and proofs to Le Lan and Liu [3]. Its contribution lies in engineering an independent, constructive, zero-float cyclotomic audit layer and Lean 4 formalization of the rational and quadratic-field reduction skeletons.

reproducibility.basis: Supplies a clear 3-command reproduction workflow, explicit MIT/CC-BY-4.0 repository archival with a SHA-256 manifest, and 16 concrete canonical certificates (Table 2) with worked rational witnesses. Minor self-containment gaps exist because Table 2 omits the exact (x,y,z,w) parameters for C02, C15, and C16 and relies on [3] for intermediate definitions.

rigor.basis: Strong verification discipline combining a Mathlib-free Lean 4.35.0 kernel (18 theorems, zero sorry, zero Classical.choice) with a zero-float Fraction-based Q[X]/(Phi_p(X)) verifier, input hardening, and 38 unit/forgery tests. Rigor is tempered because general-prime cyclotomic steps (Vandermonde, partial fractions, Galois identities) are checked only for finite prime instances (p<=23 or p<=41) rather than proved universally in Lean.

significance.basis: Provides a substantive independent verification benchmark for Le Lan and Liu's recent proof of Sun's Conjecture 3.2(i) and related determinants, auditing delicate cyclotomic-to-rational cancellations and non-trivial class-number cases (h_{-23}=3, h_{229}=3), though its impact is bounded by being an auxiliary instance-checking artifact.

potential_errors: Section 2 states Theorem 5 over arbitrary integers and Theorems 7-11 from a^2 - pb^2 = -1 alone without specifying how half-integer unit coordinates (a_p, b_p in (1/2)Z, as in C05, C09, C11, C12) are represented or cleared of denominators in the Lean 4 statements.

In Worked Witness 2 (p=13, C05), c_13 = 13/2 - (3/2)\tau_13 and det(M)^2 = -13^2\tau_13(3/2 + (1/2)\tau_13) are stated as exact in Q[\zeta_13] without fixing which sign choice of the quadratic Gauss sum \tau_13 = \pm\sqrt{13} is assumed in the narrative text.
strengths: Transparent scope and attribution: explicitly acknowledges Le Lan and Liu [3] as sole authors of the mathematical discoveries and proofs, framing this paper accurately as an independent formal-verification and exact-arithmetic audit layer.
Strong constructive formalization discipline: 18 Mathlib-free theorems in Lean 4.35.0 audited via #print axioms to depend only on [propext, Quot.sound] with zero sorry and zero Classical.choice.

Exact zero-floating-point cyclotomic arithmetic over Q[X]/(Phi_p(X)) using Python Fractions, AST-audited against float literals, true division, and float/numpy calls, paired with input hardening and 38 unit/forgery tests.

Full internal numerical and algebraic consistency across all worked witnesses (C01, C05, C06, C09, C12, C15), Table 2 metrics (C01-C16), and Figures 1-3, including non-trivial class-number witnesses h_{-23} = 3 and h_{229} = 3.
summary: This 4-page companion verification preprint constructs an independent formal and exact-arithmetic audit layer (LEGENDRE-DET-SYM-CERT-1.0) for Le Lan and Liu's proof (arXiv:2611.33667v1) of Zhi-Wei Sun's Conjecture 3.2(i) and related Legendre-symbol matrix determinants. It pairs 18 constructive, Mathlib-free Lean 4.35.0 theorems covering the universal rational reductions and quadratic-field cancellations with an AST-audited, zero-floating-point Python verifier operating over Q and exact cyclotomic fields Q[X]/(Phi_p(X)), producing 16 canonical JSON certificates (C01-C16) and 38 unit/forgery tests. All algebraic identities, determinant evaluations, unit norms, class-number cases (h_{-23}=3, h_{229}=3), and plotted quantities presented in the PDF check out accurately. As honestly disclosed by the author, this is not an end-to-end formalization of Sun's conjecture for all primes—the cyclotomic Vandermonde, partial-fraction, and Galois identities are checked only instance-by-instance on concrete primes—nor does it claim original mathematical proofs. Within its stated scope as a companion verification artifact, it is rigorous, transparent, and substantive.
weaknesses: Partial formalization coverage: universal Lean 4 proofs cover the cleared algebraic reductions and quadratic-field cancellations (18 theorems), whereas the cyclotomic Vandermonde evaluations, partial fractions, and Galois identities cited from [5] are verified only on finite prime instances in Python (up to p=23 for full Q[\zeta_p] modes and p=41 for direct rational determinants).

Limited self-containment in the 4-page PDF: intermediate objects from [3]—such as H(x), F(x), M, c_p, K, P_1, P_2, \alpha_1, \beta_1, \gamma_1, \delta_1, and Eq. (2.4)—are referenced by label without full definitions in the text, and the exact (x,y,z,w) tuples used for Table 2 entries C02, C15, and C16 are omitted from the table.

As an external PDF-only referee, the actual Lean 4 source code, Python verifier, and test suite in the linked repository were not executed or inspected directly; confidence in those artifacts rests on the PDF's explicit claims and worked numerical witnesses.
